name: xTool M2 Color Craft Laser

moduleSystem.headline: Swappable laser modules on the same M2 cabinet
moduleSystem.description: The M2 is sold with a 10W, 20W or 40W blue diode module, and every module is also sold on its own: 20W at $599 and 40W at $899 (listed on xTool's store from October 21, 2026). A 3W 1064 nm infrared module ($499) adds metal and plastic marking, and the CMYK inkjet module handles colour printing. Modules swap on the same multi-function holder; xTool says they only fit the M2.

tagline: Entry enclosed laser with CMYK color printing: xTool's 2026 mass-market craft machine
tldr: Launched May 2026, the M2 packs laser engraving, cutting, and integrated inkjet color printing into one enclosed desktop at $599. Built for everyday crafters and Etsy sellers who want color + laser without a pro CO₂ budget: not a metal-marking or production cutter.
mainObjective: Affordable enclosed laser + color print for home crafters and small shops

priceRange.note: Official xTool store, Oct 2026: 10W from $499, 20W from $899, 40W from $1,299 machine only, up to $1,849 for the 40W All-in-One bundle; the 40W 455nm diode module alone is $899 (listed from Oct 21, 2026)

pros: 10W on xTool M2 Color Craft Laser: engraving-first: photo fills and leather at moderate speeds
Integrated cabinet helps contain the beam and everyday smoke versus open-frame diodes
Upgrade path on the same cabinet: xTool sells 20W ($599) and, since late October 2026, 40W ($899) diode modules; xTool rates the 40W for 15 mm basswood and 11 mm black acrylic
cons: Clear cast acrylic and thick production cutting still favor CO₂, not diode power alone
Confirm optical wattage on the listing before you buy
The 40W module costs $899 on its own, so upgrading a 10W M2 ends up about $100 dearer than buying the 40W configuration ($1,299) from the start

faq.question: Can the xTool M2 be upgraded to 40W?
faq.answer: Yes. Since October 21, 2026 xTool sells a 40W 455nm diode module for the M2 at $899. It mounts on the same multi-function holder as the stock 10W head; xTool says its modules only fit the M2. The 20W module ($599) and the 3W 1064 nm infrared module ($499) use the same holder.

faq.question: What does the 40W module change on the M2?
faq.answer: Mostly cutting. xTool's M2 FAQ rates the 40W for 15 mm basswood plywood and 11 mm black acrylic, against 8 mm and 3 mm for the 10W, and recommends 10 mm/s instead of 4 mm/s on 3 mm black acrylic. The processing area shrinks slightly with this module, to 426 × 312 mm instead of 426 × 320 mm, and the spot is wider (0.08 × 0.1 mm).

faq.question: Buy the 40W M2 directly or upgrade a 10W later?
faq.answer: If you already know you will cut thick wood or acrylic, the 40W configuration ($1,299 machine only in October 2026) costs less than a 10W M2 ($499) plus the $899 module. The module makes sense for owners who started with the 10W and now need more cutting depth.

proTips: Budget for ink cartridges and laser-safe materials rated for both processes. Test color + laser alignment on scraps before client work.
primaryUse: 2026 entry enclosed craft system combining diode laser work with integrated color printing for gifts and small business.

editorialDepth.advantages: xTool M2 Color Craft Laser 10W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Enclosed format is easier to live with at home.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 3 mm+ cutting in production. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.
